NOTE  1  - The accompanying unaudited financial statements have been prepared in
accordance  with  Article  10  of  Regulation  S-X and do not include all of the
information  and  footnotes required by generally accepted accounting principles
for  complete  financial  statements.  In  the  opinion  of  management,  all
adjustments  considered  necessary  for  a fair presentation have been included.
These statements should be read in conjunction with the financial statements and
notes  thereto  for  Energizer  Holdings,  Inc.  (Energizer)  for the year ended
September  30,  1998,  included  elsewhere  in  this  registration  statement.

NOTE  2  -  During the nine-month period ended June 30, 1999, Energizer recorded
after-tax  provisions  for  restructuring  totaling  $5.4,  primarily related to
continued  rationalization  of  Energizer's  production  capacity.  On a pre-tax
basis,  these charges were $8.3 and consisted of cash costs of $3.3 and non-cash
charges  of  $5.0,  representing  the  write-off  of  fixed  assets.

During  the  nine-month period ended June 30, 1998, Energizer recorded after-tax
provisions  for  restructuring  of  $24.9,  primarily  related  to charges for a
voluntary early retirement option offered to most U.S. employees meeting certain
age  and  service  requirements and additional restructuring of European battery
operations.  On  a  pre-tax  basis,  these  charges  were $34.2 and consisted of
termination  benefits of $27.0, other cash costs of $6.1 and non-cash charges of
$1.1.  The  total  pre-tax and after-tax provisions were reduced by reversals of
prior  period  restructuring  charges  of  $11.9  and  $10.1,  respectively.

NOTE  3 - Energizer recorded capital loss tax benefits of $3.3 and $48.4 for the
nine  months  ended  June  30, 1999 and 1998, respectively, primarily related to
past  restructuring  actions.

NOTE  4  -  In  March  1999,  the  Board  of Directors of Ralston Purina Company
announced  its  intention  to  exit  Energizer's worldwide rechargeable Original
Equipment  Manufacturers'  (OEM) battery business to allow Energizer to focus on
its  primary  battery  business.  In September 1999, an agreement was signed for
the sale of this business, with closing expected to occur by the end of October.
The  OEM  business  is  accounted for as a discontinued operation in Energizer's
condensed  financial  statements.

Included in the Net Loss on Disposition of Discontinued Operations are operating
losses during the divestment period of $15.0, pre-tax, or $9.6, after-tax, and a
loss  on  disposition  of  $95.6,  pre-tax,  or  $64.6,  after-tax.

The  Net  Loss  from  Discontinued Operations for the nine months ended June 30,
1998  includes  an  after-tax  provision  of  $42.7,  primarily  representing an
impairment  write-down  of  lithium  ion  rechargeable  battery  assets  of this
business.

NOTE  5  -  Energizer's operations are managed via four major geographic areas -
North  America,  which  includes  the U.S. and Canada, Asia Pacific, Europe, and
South  and  Central  America.  This  structure  is  the  basis for the Company's
reportable  operating  segment information disclosed below.  Segment performance
is evaluated based on operating profit, exclusive of general corporate expenses,
research  and  development  expenses,  restructuring charges and amortization of
goodwill and intangibles.  Financial items, such as interest income and expense,
are  managed  on  a  global  basis  at  the  corporate  level.

Intersegment sales are generally valued at market-based prices and represent the
difference  between  total  sales  and  external sales as presented in the table
below.  Segment  profitability  includes  profit  on  these  intersegment sales.

NOTE  8  -  Effective  January  1,  1999, certain events occurred related to the
Ralston-sponsored  defined  contribution  plan  (the Plan), formerly a leveraged
ESOP  (ESOP),  in  which  substantially  all  regular Energizer employees in the
United  States are eligible to participate.  First, in accordance with the terms
of  the  ESOP,  all  shares  of  Ralston Purina preferred stock in the ESOP were
converted to Ralston Purina Company common stock, and the fund where participant
shares are held was renamed the Ralston ESOP Common Stock Fund.  Also, beginning
January 1, Ralston amended the Plan to provide an employer matching contribution
on  a  participant's before-tax contributions of up to 4% of compensation.  This
match  is  directed  to the ESOP Common Stock Fund but is fully diversifiable at
the  participant's  election.  Further, up to 1.75% of a participant's after-tax
contributions  are  credited  with  a  300%  match to the Ralston Purina Company
Retirement  Plan.
